features.name: Burgenland (present-day boundary)
features.accuracy: Present-day state boundary, not the territory as transferred in 1921.
features.note: Shown for orientation only. Villages were still being exchanged up to 1923, so the boundary of the time differed.

features.name: Ringstrasse (present-day streets)
features.accuracy: Present-day street centrelines, street level. The 19th-century layout isn't captured.
features.note: Shown from the 1865 opening, using today's streets. It isn't a survey of the 1865 road. The walls themselves aren't in the dataset yet.

features.name: Mürzzuschlag – Graz
features.license: Track: ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors. Endpoints: Wikidata (CC0)
features.accuracy: Today's running track, about 97.2 km, simplified to within about 15 m. Where the line was later realigned, it differs from the line as built.
features.note: The source gives the section's two ends and its opening date. The line runs by way of Bruck an der Mur.

features.name: Gloggnitz – Mürzzuschlag (Semmering)
features.license: Track: ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors. Endpoints: Wikidata (CC0)
features.accuracy: Today's running track, about 41.4 km, simplified to within about 15 m. Where the line was later realigned, it differs from the line as built.
features.note: Shown from 1854, the opening year. The source confirms the year only. The mountain line with its viaducts and tunnels is still the running line today.

features.name: Innsbruck – Bolzano (Brenner)
features.license: Track: ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors. Endpoints: Wikidata (CC0)
features.accuracy: Today's running track, about 131.8 km, simplified to within about 15 m. Where the line was later realigned, it differs from the line as built.
features.note: Shown from the 1867 opening. The Brenner Base Tunnel is still being built, so today's track is the 1867 mountain line in most places.
